findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match the one-arg method in UsernamePasswordForm — code does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method with that name in the class hierarchy is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` declared in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (lines 160-162). There is no no-arg overload in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this is a Java compilation error and the services module will not build. The fix should either call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` here or make the helper no-arg (the latter is what the rest of the change actually needs, see the finding on UsernamePasswordForm).

findings.title: Requiring a non-null user in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled disables passkey conditional UI on the initial (user-less) login page
findings.body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` includes a `user != null` condition, and both call sites pass `context.getUser()` (authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(context, error, field) at line 137). On a regular, non-re-authentication login, `context.getUser()` is null when the login page is first rendered, and it is also null when the error challenge is re-rendered after a failed username/password attempt (the user is only set on the context after successful validation, and badPasswordHandler clears it). As a result `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped exactly in the cases where it ran before this PR (previously the fill was guarded by `context.getUser() == null` or was inside the user==null else-branch). The rendered login page then lacks the WebAuthn challenge, the hidden `#webauth` form, and the `username webauthn` autocomplete attribute, so passkey autofill / discoverable-key (passwordless) login stops working for normal first-time logins — the feature only works during re-authentication. This also contradicts the PR's own tests, e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey assert `getUsernameAutocomplete() == "username webauthn"` and the presence of `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial login page where no user is set. The user check should be removed (make the helper depend only on `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`).
